local_facts.title: Southern batteries die seventeen months sooner
local_facts.claim: AAA, citing Consumer Reports data, states that vehicle batteries in the southern United States on average last 17 months less than in colder northern climates. Heat accelerates grid corrosion, the slow degradation of the internal metal grids that support the battery plates, causing reduced capacity, diminished starting power and eventual failure. AAA notes that under-hood temperatures can exceed 150 degrees in some regions.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A three-year-old battery in Savannah is a replacement candidate, and the failure usually surfaces on the first cool morning of autumn. Load-testing before replacing is the difference between fixing the car and guessing.

local_facts.title: Georgia's protection is the written estimate, not a license
local_facts.claim: Georgia does not license automotive mechanics. The state's Consumer Ed site, run by the Georgia Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division, tells drivers to get a written estimate before work begins, to make sure the estimate states that the shop will call before doing work that exceeds a specified amount or that was not agreed to, and to ask up front for all replaced parts to be returned. Suspected repair fraud is reported to the Consumer Protection Division at 404-651-8600 or 800-869-1123.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A mobile mechanic working out of a truck should meet the same standard as a shop: parts and labor on paper first, a call before exceeding it, and the old parts handed back on request.

local_facts.title: Coastal Georgia's largest employer drives a lot of one-car households
local_facts.claim: The U.S. Army Garrison Fort Stewart-Hunter Army Airfield reports 21,200 full-time soldiers, 4,350 Army civilian workers and contractors, and more than 19,000 military retirees in the Stewart-Hunter communities. Hunter Army Airfield sits inside the city of Savannah in Chatham County; Fort Stewart is about 45 miles away in Hinesville.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Military families on orders sell cars fast and buy cars fast, and a soldier's one car dying in on-post housing is a mobile-mechanic call, not a shop visit. Access to Hunter needs a visitor pass arranged in advance.

local_facts.title: Port truck traffic is moving off neighborhood streets
local_facts.claim: Georgia DOT opened the $126 million Brampton Road Connector on July 16, 2026, a four-lane highway linking the Port of Savannah's Garden City Terminal to the I-16 corridor toward Atlanta. The Georgia Ports Authority says the project removes at-grade rail crossings and truck traffic from local neighborhoods. Chatham County's population is just under 300,000 and the port is one of the three busiest in the United States.
local_facts.why_it_matters: Container trucks on I-16 and Highway 21 are part of daily driving here; the connector changes which streets in Garden City and west Savannah carry them, and where a stalled car is most dangerous.
